title: Far from These Scenes of Night
description: Far from These Scenes of Night in Tonic Solfa to AYLESBURY, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Anne Steele wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 559 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Heaven”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to AYLESBURY; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Far from these scenes of night Un-bound-ed glo-ries rise, And realms of in-fin-ite de-light, Un-known to mor-tal eyes.

lines: Far from these scenes of night
For sin, the source of mortal woe,
But glory from th' eternal throne
And lively faith and strong desire

licence: Public domain: Anne Steele died in 1778.
credits: Words by Anne Steele (1717–1778), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to AYLESBURY by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
